title: M151 · Team Companion identity, R0 (three treatments drawn; T1 fixed and atelier PASS)
summary: R0 drew three candidate identities for Team Companion and put each on the landing page (1280 and 390), a shared plan (390) and Match Day (390): T1 a ruled field sketch of the map, T2 an engraved contour sheet, T3 a schematic. T1 now has the atelier's fixes applied (straight lanes, one curved river with a bridge gap, perpendicular hatch, a real Match Day inset) and an atelier PASS on all four stills and its OG card (critique-r0b-t1.md). T2, T3, their OG cards and the 'paper' light still (C) are NOT atelier-critiqued; the T1 share OG variant is FIX for R1. The Match Day 'both sides' marks facing' field card was dropped on the atelier's ruling: in a best of 3 neither team owns a side (MD-1); the inset now floats top right as in T2 and T3. Also built: nine original marks for the five roles and objectives (atelier PASS, in the /design gallery), a reMarkable template if you want to draw them yourself, the lock-in motion for a draft pick (fixed at 390; the 1280 strip is stale), a static win/loss stamp. All of it is gallery and planning files; nothing reached the app's real pages or production. CI: check job (fmt, clippy ssr+wasm32, lib and integration tests) and image job green on da342bc, run 38986274881; e2e still running when the round stopped.. One legal question for your adviser: may a fan tool draw its own role/objective marks that resemble in-game icons? Ours are original geometry, deliberately distant. Report: REPORT-R0.md.

questions.text: Which treatment should carry the identity (react)? The T1 stills are after the atelier's fixes, with an atelier PASS (critique-r0b-t1.md); T2 and T3 are not critiqued. Also the result stamp: the brief said 'drawn once', the atelier ruled 'static at first paint' (critique-r0-t1.md). Pick the fourth chip to choose T1 with the stamp drawn once.

chips.label: T1 field sketch
chips.consequence: R1 takes T1 forward with the R1 refinements (R1-a to R1-d); T2 and T3 are dropped. The stamp stays static at first paint (the atelier's ruling).

chips.label: T2 contour
chips.consequence: R1 takes the engraved contour sheet forward: first atelier critique, then fixes; T1 and T3 dropped. Stamp static at first paint.

chips.label: T3 schematic
chips.consequence: R1 takes the schematic forward: first atelier critique, then fixes; T1 and T2 dropped. Stamp static at first paint.

chips.label: T1, but stamp drawn once
chips.consequence: As 'T1 field sketch', and the stamp gets a one-time entrance (never replayed), overriding the atelier. With any other pick the stamp is static at first paint (critique-r0-t1.md).

questions.recommend: T1 field sketch, stamp static. T1 is the only treatment critiqued and passed; it says 'League team' without words. Static keeps the server-rendered first frame complete and lock-in the only signature motion.

questions.text: Role and objective marks (react): draw them yourself on the reMarkable template, or take the nine marks the atelier passed?

chips.label: Draw them myself (reMarkable template)
chips.consequence: You draw nine marks on marks-template.pdf; IMPORT.md turns them into public/marks/*.svg, then an atelier check at 16 px.

chips.label: Take the atelier set
chips.consequence: The nine drawn marks ship as they are (after the legal answer and the DESIGN amendment).

questions.recommend: Take the atelier set. It passed at 16 px beside its word; your hand can replace single marks later through the same template.

questions.text: Lead-figure grammar (react): one figure, one sentence, one action on landing, share and Match Day. Adopt it as the page rule?

chips.label: Yes
chips.consequence: DESIGN.md gets the rule; R1 rebuilds the three surfaces around it.

chips.label: No
chips.consequence: Pages keep today's layout; the identity is applied as art only.

questions.recommend: Yes. It is what makes the stills read in a second, and it matches the one-primary-action rule already in DESIGN.

questions.text: C paper still (react): a light 'paper' version of the share page. Does it convince you enough to plan a light theme?

chips.label: Convinced
chips.consequence: A later round plans a paper theme; chalk becomes deep olive and the danger hover rule changes.

chips.label: Not convinced
chips.consequence: One dark theme stays; the still is archived.

questions.recommend: Not convinced, for now. It costs a rule change and a second token set, and it has had no critique yet.
